title: CWE-89: SQL Injection
text: SQL Injection occurs when untrusted input is concatenated directly into a SQL query. Always use parameterized queries or an ORM's query builder instead of string formatting/concatenation. In Python, use cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s', (user_id,)) rather than f-strings. Validate and allow-list input where possible, and apply least-privilege DB accounts.

title: CWE-78: OS Command Injection
text: Command injection happens when user input reaches a shell command. Avoid os.system/subprocess with shell=True and string-built commands. Prefer subprocess.run with a list of arguments and shell=False, and validate/allow-list inputs. Never pass unsanitized input to eval/exec either.

title: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
text: Hard-coded API keys, passwords, or tokens in source code are a critical risk if the repo is ever exposed. Store secrets in environment variables or a secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault) and load them at runtime. Rotate any credential that has ever been committed to version control.

title: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
text: MD5 and SHA1 are not collision-resistant and must not be used for password hashing or integrity-critical signatures. Use bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2 for password storage, and SHA-256/SHA-3 (with proper HMAC/keying) for integrity checks.

title: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
text: Deserializing untrusted data with pickle.loads, yaml.load (without SafeLoader), or Java's ObjectInputStream can lead to remote code execution. Use safe formats like JSON, or yaml.safe_load, and validate schema before deserializing. Never unpickle data from an untrusted source.

title: CWE-79: Cross-Site Scripting
text: Reflected/stored XSS occurs when untrusted input is rendered into HTML/JS without escaping. Use templating engines with auto-escaping enabled, avoid innerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML with raw user input, and apply a Content-Security-Policy header as defense in depth.

title: CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
text: All external input (query params, form fields, headers, file uploads) should be validated against an explicit allow-list of expected types, lengths, and formats before use. Fail closed: reject unexpected input rather than attempting to sanitize it heuristically.

title: CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password
text: Do not embed default or hard-coded passwords in application code, config files checked into git, or Docker images. Inject credentials at deploy time via environment variables or an orchestrator secret store.

title: OWASP: Insufficient Logging & Monitoring
text: Security-relevant events (auth failures, access-control failures, input validation failures) should be logged with enough context to support incident response, without logging sensitive data like passwords or tokens in plaintext.

title: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment
text: Files, especially those containing secrets or executable scripts, should be created with the least permissive mode necessary (e.g. 0600 for secret files). Avoid chmod 777 or world-writable directories for application data.

title: Secure & Maintainable Error Handling
text: Avoid bare except clauses that swallow all exceptions silently; catch specific exception types and log context. Never leak stack traces or internal error details directly to end users/API responses in production.

title: Maintainability: Avoid Magic Numbers and Duplication
text: Repeated literal values and duplicated logic blocks reduce maintainability and increase the risk of inconsistent fixes. Extract them into named constants or shared functions.
